newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1.00 - private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1.00 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were steady to mostly $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower following more than adequate marketings on Wednesday, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
"We have what we need for today's kill and have about 70 percent of needs covered for Friday already," a buyer in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota market said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $58.50 to $59.50 at plants. Illinois hogs sold $0.50-$1.00 lower at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants.
A few packers reportedly were willing to pay $60.00 in Illinois for top quality hogs, dealers there said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $58.50 to $59.00 in the country and $59.50 to $60.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold steady at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $60.00 to $61.00 at plants. The Indiana/Ohio market had a reported top of $60.75 on Wednesday, but dealers said $61.00 was paid by at least one plant for quality hogs.
Marketings in the Midwest turned active late Tuesday and Wednesday as this week's heat lost some of its sizzle and owners sensed that cash hog prices were near a top.
